corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: Stance 130 - Speculative decoding changes the arithmetic intensity of decode and therefore changes which parallel axis is cheap.

Common frame (applies to every stance below).
Assumptions (must be restated by the answering engineer, not inherited silently):
A1. Single node, 8 GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node; inter-node paths only appear where a stance says so explicitly.
A2. Decode-dominant, latency-sensitive serving: the SLO is TTFT p95 and TPOT (inter-token latency) p95, never a mean.
A3. Model weights fit in aggregate HBM with at least 20% KV-cache headroom at target concurrency.
A4. Exactly one variable moves per arm: no simultaneous change of quantization, batching policy, or speculative decoding.
Mechanism, stated plainly:
- Tensor parallelism (TP) shards every layer's GEMMs. Each transformer block needs two all-reduces (after attention out-projection and after the MLP down-projection), so decode carries L * 2 * allreduce_latency of synchronous cost, where L is the layer count. TP is latency-additive in collectives but capacity- and bandwidth-multiplying: per-GPU weight bytes and per-GPU KV bytes both fall by the TP degree.
- Pipeline parallelism (PP) shards layers into stages. Per token it adds only (PP-1) small point-to-point hidden-state sends, which are cheap, but a single request serializes through all stages and the bubble fraction is (PP-1)/(micro_batches + PP-1). At low concurrency there are too few in-flight micro-batches to fill the pipeline, so PP loses badly on single-request latency.
Boundary conditions that flip the answer:
- B1. On NVLink-class fabric, small-message all-reduce latency is in the single-digit microseconds and TP up to 8 is normally latency-viable. Over PCIe-only or across nodes on RoCE/IB the same collective's latency floor rises roughly an order of magnitude and TP stops paying past TP=2 (ESTIMATE; derivation: decode all-reduce payload is hidden_size * dtype_bytes per token per layer, which is small, so the collective is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and the per-hop latency floor dominates).
- B2. If the model cannot fit on one GPU, sharding is mandatory and the question reduces to which axis, not whether.
- B3. Under high, steady concurrency the PP bubble amortizes and PP becomes competitive on throughput per GPU while still losing on single-request latency.
Default recommendation: use TP inside the node up to the point where collective cost stops being repaid by reduced per-GPU memory traffic; use PP only to cross a node boundary or to fit a model TP alone cannot fit. PP is not a latency optimization.

Only values read out of named benchmark artifacts may be labelled MEASURED. This review reports no MEASURED values, because no benchmark was executed for it.

Speculative decoding replaces one-token-at-a-time decode with a draft-then-verify loop in which the target model scores several candidate tokens in a single forward pass. That converts a chain of tiny, latency-bound steps into fewer, wider steps, which raises arithmetic intensity and amortises each layer's collectives over more accepted tokens. Tensor parallelism, whose cost is a fixed per-layer synchronous all-reduce, is repaid better under speculation than under plain decode. Pipeline parallelism sees the opposite pressure: the verify step is still one logical request walking every stage, so the bubble is unchanged while the per-step work grows. Falsifiable hypothesis H130: enabling speculative decoding will shrink the TTFT-normalised TPOT penalty attributed to tensor parallelism by a larger relative margin than it shrinks the penalty attributed to pipeline parallelism, at fixed acceptance rate (ESTIMATE; derivation: TP collective cost per layer is roughly constant per forward pass, so cost per accepted token falls with the mean accepted-token count, whereas the PP bubble fraction (PP-1)/(micro_batches+PP-1) does not depend on tokens accepted per pass). Controlled experiment: Run four arms: TP-only and PP-only, each with speculation off and on, holding draft model, acceptance threshold, batching policy and quantisation fixed. Log mean accepted tokens per verify pass per arm and normalise all latency numbers by it. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

In decode the dominant device cost is streaming weights out of HBM, and weight-only quantisation reduces those bytes roughly in proportion to the bit-width ratio. Collectives, however, operate on activations, which are usually kept at higher precision and are unaffected. So quantisation shrinks the numerator of the compute term while leaving the tensor-parallel synchronisation term intact, raising the fraction of step time spent in all-reduce. A tensor-parallel degree that looked free at full precision can become the visible bottleneck once weights are compressed. Falsifiable hypothesis H131: moving from full-precision to weight-only quantised weights will increase the share of per-token step time spent in all-reduce for the tensor-parallel arm, and the absolute TPOT gain from quantisation will be smaller at higher tensor degree than at lower tensor degree (ESTIMATE; derivation: per-GPU weight bytes scale as total_weight_bytes / TP and shrink further by the quantisation ratio, while activation all-reduce payload is hidden_size * dtype_bytes per layer and is invariant to weight precision, so the ratio of collective time to compute time rises). Controlled experiment: Sweep tensor degree over at least two values, crossed with quantised and unquantised weights, four cells total, holding batching policy, speculation setting and sequence-length distribution fixed. Capture a collective-level profile in every cell. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

Prefill is a large, compute-dense batched matrix multiply over the whole prompt: it has high arithmetic intensity and tolerates collectives well, so it scales acceptably with tensor degree. Decode is a sequence of thin, memory-bound steps in which the same collective is paid per layer per token and is latency-bound. Optimising one layout for both phases means accepting a setting that is wrong for at least one of them. Prefill-decode disaggregation exists precisely to let each phase pick its own degree, at the cost of transferring KV state between the two pools. Under continuous batching, requests join and leave the running batch at token granularity, so the effective batch a given decode step sees is a moving quantity set by arrival rate, admission policy and preemption. Tensor parallelism divides both weight bytes and KV bytes across ranks, so raising the degree buys KV headroom. That headroom is not a comfort metric: when the cache is exhausted the scheduler must preempt or recompute, and those events show up as large latency spikes in exactly the tail the SLO governs. Chunked prefill splits a long prompt into pieces so that prefill work can be interleaved with ongoing decode steps rather than blocking them.
